clue.text: In so disconcerting a way, English doctor hanging one at a time

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
an arras is a tapestry wall hanging
singly means one by one

explanation.surface: Someone describes an awkward scene where a doctor dangles people one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: ARRAS, a tapestry hung on a wall (Polonius hides behind one in Hamlet), is the 'hanging', not an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done embarrassingly is done in a way that causes awkward discomfort.

clue.text: Formerly, reticent person I found inside Yell

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or formerly

indicators.note: found inside says one piece is placed within the other here

parts.note: a clam is slang for someone who keeps tight-lipped

explanation.surface: A once-shy person turns up within the Shetland island of Yell.
explanation.walkthrough: Yell is one of the Shetland Islands in the surface, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, a synonym of shouting.

clue.text: Breakdown of deliveries?

parts.note: read as the cricket record listing a bowler's overs, maidens, runs and wickets, not a failure of the post

explanation.surface: A complaint that the post or parcel service has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; the analysis records each bowler's figures, a British game unfamiliar to many.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler's figures break down how their balls bowled went in terms of runs and wickets.

clue.text: Track this bird

definitions.meaning: the metal track a train runs on
a ... is a marsh bird such as the water ...

explanation.surface: An instruction to follow a bird's trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway track is made of rails, and the rail is also a family of wading birds.

clue.text: Compensation for what happens at midday

definitions.meaning: making ... means compensating for a wrong
at noon the morning, a.m., finishes

explanation.surface: Someone seeks recompense for something that occurs at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Amends are reparation for harm; split, the word says the morning stops at twelve noon.

clue.text: Patient, kicking up endless fuss, could be free to run…

indicators.note: in a down clue kicking up turns the word upwards, so it reads backwards
endless means the final letter of the word fuss is dropped
could be suggests the letters of free may be rearranged into another form

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A patient making a scene could be free to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicking up' reverses FUS (fuss without its end) to SUF; 'could be' rearranges FREE to FERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient is a person enduring an illness, one who suffers.

clue.text: … but this one never gets off, of course

definitions.text: but this one never gets off, of course

parts.words: but this one never gets off, of course
parts.note: read as a racehorse that never leaves the start of the course, continuing the previous clue's running

explanation.surface: Following on from a runner, this one obviously never gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the clue before; 'of course' means a racecourse, not 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that fails to start a race, or a plan that has no chance of success.

clue.text: Scenery-painter?

parts.note: read as someone who paints views of the countryside, but also hints at a stage scenery painter

explanation.surface: A question about who paints the backdrops.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter of rural views and natural vistas.

clue.text: Carry on nursing, though it is a subject of strain

definitions.meaning: to ... is to keep looking after someone
the cord joining muscle to bone is often strained in sport

explanation.surface: Keep caring for a patient, even though the work is stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though it is' is a link phrase between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, the word says keep tending; whole, it is the fibrous cord that sportsmen often pull or strain.

clue.text: Jersey, say, to conceal skin

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of dairy cattle, an example of a cow
to hide is to conceal

explanation.surface: Wearing a jumper in order to hide one's skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like a sweater (a jumper) but is the Channel Island breed of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather made from cattle is an animal skin.

clue.text: Money matters of one engaged about noon

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a fiance is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: Money worries of a betrothed person around lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance is the management of money, monetary affairs.

clue.text: A big hit turned back the alliance

indicators.note: turned back says the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: in cricket a six is a big hit clearing the boundary

explanation.surface: A major success sent the coalition into retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: A SIX is cricket's biggest scoring shot, over the boundary without bouncing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan.

clue.text: Verdi dates wantonly plugged

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly or unruly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: The composer Verdi's concert dates were shamelessly promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a product is to promote or publicise it.

clue.text: Feeling for T in semaphore, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about the flag signal used to represent the letter T.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'in' are link words; T and SEMAPHORE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere is the mood or ambience of a place, its prevailing tone.

clue.text: Potent stout?

definitions.meaning: stout in the sense of strong and sturdy

explanation.surface: A strong beer described in a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean powerful and strong; stout can mean robust or brave.

clue.text: Writer, embracing wayward Maria, produces an apple

indicators.note: embracing means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a pen is something used for writing

indicators.note: wayward means straying, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: An author hugging a wilful woman named Maria comes up with an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: ARMAI, the anagram of MARIA by 'wayward', goes inside PEN after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearmain is an old English variety of dessert fruit, as in Worcester Pearmain.

clue.text: A number limit Tate restoration with bitter quarrel

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
an end is a limit or boundary

indicators.note: restoration means reworking, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Restoring a picture at the Tate gallery leads to a feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restoration' turns TATE into ETTA; the Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged feud between families or rivals.

clue.text: Survival of great leader in royal house

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the name of the dynasty

parts.note: Hanover was the German royal house that ruled Britain from George I

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word great

explanation.surface: A great ruler survives within a royal dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is something remaining from an earlier time, a relic.

clue.text: Ivy adhere all over the place?

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ivy clings everywhere it grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the botanical genus name of the climbing plant.

clue.text: Wild rat?

definitions.meaning: to rat is to abandon or betray one's side

explanation.surface: An untamed rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is a wild uninhabited region; to rat on allies is to abandon them.

clue.text: Profits, thanks to double books

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
Kings is a pair of Old Testament books, First and Second

explanation.surface: Earnings rose thanks to keeping two sets of accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double books' suggests fraudulent bookkeeping; it is the two Books of Kings in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are money received, a shop's receipts or earnings.

clue.text: Declare at cricket

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A batsman declaring an innings closed during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a side can 'declare' its innings over, the surface's sense; a Test match is the longest international form.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to state formally or bear witness to.

clue.text: I dial a dept, about waste

indicators.note: about signals moving the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone phones a department about rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilapidate is to squander or let fall into ruin.

clue.text: Centre-half to take opening kick? That's a long journey!

indicators.note: half here takes the latter half of the word Centre
opening means the first letter of the word kick

explanation.surface: A footballer in central defence takes the kick-off of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre-half' looks like a football position but splits: the last half of CENTRE, TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is an arduous journey, often on foot.

clue.text: Henry with song that grows on one

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Henry's song is one that grows on you.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grows on a person's head and body.

clue.text: Detail of ghastly spectre

indicators.note: ghastly means horribly distorted, so the letters are disfigured into another order

explanation.surface: A close look at a hideous ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: A respect is a particular point or aspect, as in 'in every respect'.

clue.text: Kinsman loses head in high spirits

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a relation is a family member, a kinsman

explanation.surface: A relative is beheaded while in a joyful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration.

clue.text: O, to sit is rather difficult, having this condition

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are in a troublesome state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sufferer groans that sitting down is rather hard with this ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the patient's own lament; 'having' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A degenerative joint disease that makes movements such as sitting painful.
